Boxed intertwining proved: equal source moments S1* T1^n S1 = S2* T2^n S2 on a source-minimal (stabilized) Krylov packet give a unitary U with U S1 = S2 and U T1 = T2 U; uniqueness on the stabilized packet as source_cyclic_unique (any two intertwiners agree on the Krylov data). Disclosures: both realizations carried on one finite index type (two abstract spaces of equal stabilized packet dimension embed there); moments assumed at all orders (the finite window 0 <= n <= 2r+1 recovers all orders by Cayley-Hamilton, standard, cited); self-adjoint transports; stabilization enters as surjectivity of the depth-d Krylov matrix.

lem:small-transverse-step-master.title: Exact small transverse step
lem:small-transverse-step-master.note: NCG/Flagship/TransverseStep.lean. The boxed pulse identity exp(-i eta sigma_y/2) = Z(a) N_theta(beta) Z(c) proved exactly for 0 < theta <= pi/2, 0 <= eta <= 2 theta, with s = sin(eta/2)/sin theta, beta = 2 arcsin s, z = cos(beta/2) - i cos theta sin(beta/2), phi = arg z, a = phi + pi/2, c = phi - pi/2. The range condition gives 0 <= s <= 1 (sine monotonicity on [-pi/2, pi/2]); |z|^2 = 1 - sin^2 theta sin^2(beta/2) = cos^2(eta/2) (exact trig bookkeeping); the polar form e^{-i phi} z = cos(eta/2) and its conjugate give the diagonal entries, and e^{-+ i pi/2} = -+ i with sin theta sin(beta/2) = sin(eta/2) give the off-diagonal entries. The pulses are the standard SU(2) matrices in closed form (Z(phi) = diag(e^{-i phi/2}, e^{i phi/2}), N_theta(beta) = exp(-i beta (cos theta sigma_z + sin theta sigma_x)/2) - disclosed closed-form rendering). The SU(2) conjugacy determination of the lower row is replaced by the direct computation of all four entries.

cor:polar-Gram-resource-master.title: Sharp Gram--resource law for the polar quarter-root
cor:polar-Gram-resource-master.note: NCG/Flagship/ClusterCompiler.lean. The two-axis Bloch Gram [[1, cos theta],[cos theta, 1]] has certified eigenpairs (1 - cos theta, (1,-1)) and (1 + cos theta, (1,1)), the boxed floor identity lambda_min = 1 - cos theta = 2 sin^2(theta/2), and the boxed count identity ceil(pi/(4 theta)) = ceil(pi/(8 arcsin sqrt(lambda_min/2))) for 0 < theta <= pi (via arcsin sqrt((1-cos theta)/2) = theta/2). The identification k_pol = k_* and the length bound L_pol <= 2 k_pol + 1 are the pulse-count semantics of thm:optimal-transverse-pulse-master (not in scope here; disclosed).

lem:cluster-common-dwell-master.title: Sharp one-dwell cluster centre
lem:cluster-common-dwell-master.note: NCG/Flagship/ClusterCompiler.lean. Boxed minimax identity proved in two-sided form: at the centre t* = pi/(2(mu- + mu+)) every cluster frequency mu in [mu-, mu+] has phase error |t* mu - pi/4| <= (pi/4)(mu+ - mu-)/(mu+ + mu-), and for every dwell time t the maximum endpoint error is at least this value (hence the inf-max equals it; the sup over the interval is attained at endpoints since the error is affine in mu - rendered via the endpoint maximum, disclosed).

thm:cluster-Bernstein-filter-master.title: Inter-cluster Bernstein filter
thm:cluster-Bernstein-filter-master.note: Both boxed bounds proved for an abstract Delta^{-1}-Lipschitz [0,1]-valued cluster indicator f on [lam_-, lam_+]: positivity 0 <= p_{a,n} <= 1 (convex weights) and the error bound |p_{a,n}(lam) - f(lam)| <= R/(2 Delta sqrt n) at every point of the window, via Mathlib bernstein.variance, discrete Cauchy-Schwarz, and x(1-x) <= 1/4. The piecewise-affine construction of f_a from the disjoint cluster intervals (which realizes the Lipschitz hypothesis) and the merging remark are prose.

prop:semantic-moment-error-master.title: Certified semantic-moment inversion
prop:semantic-moment-error-master.note: NCG/Flagship/CertifiedInversion.lean. The boxed propagated error bar: for exact and measured systems Vp = m, V-hat p-hat = m-hat with eta = ||V^{-1}||*||Delta V|| < 1, ||p-hat - p|| <= (||V^{-1}||/(1-eta))(||Delta m|| + ||Delta V||*||p||) (semantic_moment_error), proved on a normed space with the operator norm via the identity (1 + V^{-1}DeltaV)(p-hat - p) = V^{-1}(Delta m - Delta V p) and the elementary Neumann lower bound (1-eta)||x|| <= ||x + Tx||. The perturbed solution p-hat enters as a hypothesis solving the measured system (its existence for eta < 1 is the Neumann invertibility, prose); the closing sentence about depth-two determinants and loading differences is the prose consequence (disclosed).
